# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 58 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 58 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_058_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 5, Part 4 — On True Fasting and the Keeping of Commandments

**58:1** "Lord," I said, "I wish to learn also the meaning of the fasting. How should we fast?" "Listen," he said. "The fast you observe is this: when you fast on the appointed days, do not eat at all until the ninth hour. But the foods you would have eaten on that day, eat them on the day of the fast after the ninth hour. Whatever you save from your foods, give it to a widow or an orphan or to someone in need. So you humble yourself, so that the one who receives may be satisfied from your humbling, and may pray to the Lord on your behalf."

**58:2** "If therefore you do this fast as I have shown you, your sacrifice will be acceptable before God, and this fast will be written down, and the service performed in this way is beautiful and joyful and acceptable to the Lord."

**58:3** "These things you shall observe with your children and with all your house. And when you observe them, you shall be blessed. And all those who hear these words and observe them shall be blessed; and whatever they ask of the Lord, they shall receive."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the practical fasting instruction that balances the theological allegory of Similitude 5.*
